content:
Operation Southern Surge, a multi-agency enforcement operation in South Texas, ran from October 29 to November 2 and has concluded, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement cited by KGNS.

The operation led to 89 arrests, KGNS reported. Seizures reported included 11 pounds of fentanyl, 30 pounds of cocaine and 26 pounds of methamphetamine, along with $3.1 million, 11 search warrants served, 4 seizures conducted and more than 1,100 rounds of ammunition.

The operation covered South Texas, including the Rio Grande Valley and the Laredo area, with locations named including the Laredo Port of Entry, the Colombia Port of Entry, Laredo, Rio Grande City and McAllen, according to KGNS.

Adriana Arce, a spokesperson for the Laredo Port of Entry, said the operation was a multi-agency effort and that U.S. Customs and Border Protection worked alongside Homeland Security Investigations, the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Homeland Security Task Force, KGNS reported. Arce said more details on arrests and seizures would be released as they become available. No individual arrested person was named in the report, and no individual charges were listed — only aggregate arrest and seizure figures.

title: Operation Southern Surge Ends With 89 Arrests Across South Texas
